20_marg311: Also in chapter 1, before the middle of it: and they roasted the phase with fire as was fitting, and boiled the victims in emolis [so the edition] and pots with good will, that is, willingly and cheerfully. But it seems that 'benevolentia' would better be said in the feminine gender, so that it is a manner of speaking. Hence another translation has: with a sweet odor.
20_marg312: And the works of Josias were set right in the sight of the Lord his God in a heart full of metuentia, that is, reverence, so that it is of the feminine gender; hence another translation has: in a heart full of piety.
20_marg313: What have I to do with thee, king of Juda? I am not sent by the Lord. [As if to say]: Thus [sent], but not against thee. Hence there follows: For my war is upon the Euphrates; making haste I go down. In 2 Paralipomenon 35 he has this more fully.
20_marg314: Also, d. He did not heed the word of the prophet from the mouth of the Lord, but set battle against him in the plain of Macedo. Another translation says that the prophet who says these things was Jeremias. For 'Macedo' some wrongly have 'Matedo' or 'Metedem'. Hence in Theodotius [so the edition] two false things are read, where it is said: 'The towns of Juda wept for the setting of Josue; the fountain and the tree detest the plains of Macedo.' There 'Josue' is wrongly put for 'Josias', and 'Macedonia' for 'Magedon'. And this is because students of grammar do not know the histories of the Bible.
20_marg315: Also, e. And he fined the nation a hundred talents of silver and one talent of gold. Another translation has: and ten talents of gold.
20_marg316: Also, e. And Joachim bound the magistrates; Zarachele his brother, seizing him, he brought back Egypto, that is, into Egypt. Hence another translation: But seizing Zacharias his brother he brought him into Egypt.
20_marg317: Also, e. And binding him in a bond of brass. This is the true reading, as appears in another translation.
20_marg318: Also, f. Now when he was appointed he was eighteen years old. So it is corrected; and in 2 Paralipomenon 36, as in 4 Kings 24, it is said: of eighteen years.
20_marg319: Also, f. Also, a little after: when he was one and twenty years old. Some wrongly have twenty-eight.
20_marg320: Also, g. But they scoffed in their corners [so the edition: 'angulis'], and on the day God spoke they were mocking his prophets. Another translation: But they mocked his angels.
20_marg321: Also, g. For their irreligions. Otherwise: or for their impieties. Also, g. And he commanded the kings of the Chaldeans to come up. Another translation agrees with this reading.
20_marg322: Also: And all the holy vessels of the Lord and the royal storehouses they took up and carried into Babylon. Another translation inserts: and the ark; which does not seem true, as appears in 2 Machabees 2.
20_marg323: So Pharao, Assuerus and Herod; on the contrary, Luke 14.
20_marg324: Also, e. O men, why are not women stronger? What follows in certain [copies], Great is the earth and high is the heaven, which do these things, is superfluous in this place and does not pertain to the matter, since the same comes a little after, where moravit [so the edition] to speak of truth, [unclear in the edition: "ut alia translatio hec habet non sit"].
20_marg325: The Son of man hath not where to lay his head.
20_marg326: Also, e. With her there is no accepting of persons nor differences, but she does what is just to all, the unjust and the wicked. Iniustis can be one word or two. Another translation: She departs from all the wicked and deceitful.
20_marg327: Also, f. which Cyrus set apart when he mated Babylon. Some wrongly have mactavit, that is, slew, which is nothing to the point. For matare is here put for to discomfit: a word common among those who play at chess [so the edition: 'scoqos'] and dice, because each intends to mate the other. Another translation: after he laid waste Babylon, which is the same, but is not in use.
20_marg328: 5.a. And after these things the chiefs of the districts were picked to go up by their houses and by their tribes. Some have 'were chosen', which is the same.
20_marg329: Also, a. The priests, the sons of Phinees, son of Aaron: Jesus son of Iosebeth. Here is a raised point. There follows: Joachim son of Zorobabel, son of Salathiel, of the house of David, of the stock of Phares, of the tribe of Juda. And here is a raised point. Who, namely Zorobabel, spoke wonderful words under Darius king of the Persians in the second year of his reign, in the first month Nisan; supply: day. The sense is confused unless it is pointed so.
20_marg330: Also, a. And they returned into Jerusalem and the remaining part of Judea, every one into his city, who came with Zorobabel and Jesus. Here is a raised point, because all who follow in this verse are of the nominative case, but in the first [book] of Esdras they are ablatives. With this reading also the first chapter of Esdras agrees, and another translation, which says: and they returned into Jerusalem and into all the cities of Judea, etc.
20_marg331: Also, b. And the number of them by their nations and of their governors; supply 'this is', as another translation has, which says: This is the number of the nation and of the princes of the Jews. Some wrongly have 'by their gentiles'. The names and numbers of all who follow in this place we do not set down, so that they may be better corrected by the more studious; for as in the Hebrew and in ancient and modern books Esdras and Nehemias cannot agree in names and numbers through the fault of scribes, so also here. Note however that from this place, 'the sons of Phares', as far as 'and of these the kindred was sought, written in the register', all the 'sons' are nominative plural. In this interval, however: 'but the porters', supply 'were', the sons of Esnomu, the sons of Azer, the sons of Amon, the sons of Acuba, the sons of Atita, the sons of Tobi, in all one hundred thirty-nine; here let there be a verse. The priests serving in the temple, supply 'were', the sons of Sel and the rest who follow as far as the sons of Pedon; here is a verse.
20_marg332: Salomon: here is a small point, and it is put absolutely so that the following relative may have place. His sons, that is, his boys or servants, were those who follow, the sons of Asophos and the rest. Hence also in the following verse it is said: all serving the holy [place], namely the temple, and the boys of Salomon, four hundred eighty-two. Salomon here is of the genitive case.
20_marg333: There follows: these are the sons who went up from Thelmela, Thelarsa, that is, from Babylon. Some wrongly have Athehnel and Thersas, as though these were two places or two words, as appears from the Hebrew in Esdras 2; and there some, as also here, wrongly thought that Dethel and Mela and Thel and Arsa are the names of four men who went up, whereas it is one word in the Interpretations.
20_marg334: Also, d. Whose height shall be sixty cubits and its breadth sixty cubits.
20_marg335: 7.a. Then Sisennes, under-governor of Celessiria and Phenice, and Sarrabuzanes, and his companions, etc.
20_marg336: Also 8.a.: I, judging more humanely, even in benefits, etc.; that is, not only not harming but even conferring benefits. Or it can be said: in benefits, that is, doing good, as they are called benefactors in eum [so the edition].
20_marg337: and teach all who shall know the law of God. Another translation adds: and those who do not know. Hence Esdras 7.g.: 'But teach the unlearned also freely.' There follows: that whoever shall have transgressed the law be diligently punished, whether by death or by torment, or also by a fine of money, or by banishment, that is, exile. Also in Esdras 7.g. it is said: 'Whoever will not do the law of thy God and the law of the king diligently'. And so this word, 'diligently', can be construed with what precedes or with what follows: so that whoever sins diligently, that is, knowingly, is diligently punished. Another translation has here: the law of God and of the king, as in Esdras.
20_marg338: Of the sons of Phinees, Gersonius: some have it wrongly.
20_marg339: Of the sons of Phares, as appears in Esdras 8.a.
20_marg340: Of the sons of Saphatias, Zacharias [son] of Micheli, that is, son of Micheli, as it is said: James [son] of Zebedee, etc. With him eighty men.
20_marg341: Of the sons of Job, Abdias [son] of Iezeli.
20_marg342: These leaders and men of skill: another translation: overseers.
20_marg343: For the sake of protection against our adversaries. Another translation: for protection.
20_marg344: Lord, I am confounded and prescriptus [so the edition] in thy sight.
20_marg345: And when Jechonias [son] of Ieeli had cried out, that is, son of Ieeli. v. [so the edition]
20_marg346: And of the sons of Iolun, Mathanias. Another translation: Of the sons of Olim, Mathanias, etc. Here ends the correction of the apocryphal Esdras.
20_interl243: by a mystery, as there: who gave you the spirit
